Placeholder/What's Fake: ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-04 for user-reported 'shake sometimes works, sometimes doesn't' (on a real physical phone, not the emulator). Two real bugs: (1) reversalCount was tallied against a FIXED wall-clock window (windowStartTime reset every exactly 1000ms) rather than a rolling window - a genuine shake could have its accumulated reversals thrown away mid-shake purely because of when, relative to that fixed clock tick, the user happened to start shaking. (2) The magnitude gate used to COUNT a reversal (thresholdMs2 / 2f, half the real threshold) didn't match the gate used to actually TRIGGER (thresholdMs2, the full threshold) - an inconsistent, overly narrow combination. (3) The proximity-sensor pocket-guard could report a stale/incorrect 'covered' reading on some real devices (unlike the emulator's fake sensor, which likely never showed the symptom) and permanently block detection depending on phone orientation/model.
What You Need To Do: FIXED: reversal counting now uses a rolling deadline (extended by each qualifying reversal, not reset by a fixed clock tick) and the same magnitude threshold for both counting and triggering. The proximity-sensor gate was removed entirely rather than made more forgiving, since it's an inherently unreliable signal across different phone hardware and the manual 'Report an Issue' button already exists as a guaranteed-reliable fallback trigger. If shake still feels inconsistent after this fix, the next lever to pull is the Settings screen's shake-sensitivity slider (lower = easier to trigger) or increasing MIN_REVERSALS tolerance further.
Priority: RESOLVED - needs real-device retest to confirm
